correction_to_the_task_anchor.evidence: over C_5^2 there are 18 classes; 4 of them have max multiplicity 3, so shape A (which needs multiplicity 4) cannot hold. Brute force over all 480 ordered bases: 0 classes fit neither shape.
correction_to_the_task_anchor.what_was_stated: the rank-2 form e^{p-1} * prod_{i=1}^{p-1}(a_i e + f) [shape A]
correction_to_the_task_anchor.why_incomplete: the full statement needs a second shape e^{p-2} * prod_{i=1}^{p}(a_i e + f) with sum a_i = 1 [shape B]

prior_art.rank_2: classical -- Property B (Gao-Geroldinger; proved for prime n by Reiher), with the Bhowmik-Schlage-Puchta / Gao-Geroldinger description of maximal zero-sum-free sequences over C_n^2
prior_art.rank_3: NOT known. Complete inverse results were found only for special families (Schmid, EJC 18 (2011) #P33 for C_2^2 + C_2n; Bhowmik-Schlage-Puchta 2007 for C_3+C_3+C_3d). The literature explicitly motivates the rank-2 structure by the fact that rank-3 Davenport is unresolved in general.
prior_art.verdict: no source gave a structural classification for C_p^3; this is new territory

problem: the inverse Davenport problem for C_5^3: classify maximal zero-sum-free sequences (length d = 12) and minimal zero-sum sequences of maximal length (D = 13), up to GL(3,5)

proved.P1: sigma(S) != 0 for every zero-sum-free S, so U = S*(-sigma(S)) has length 13 and is a MINIMAL zero-sum sequence

P2_inductive_reduction.boundary: the argument fails at multiplicity 3, where j = 1,2 are unblocked
P2_inductive_reduction.proof: if a sub-multiset T' of T sums to 0 in G/<g> then sigma(T') = j g for some j in 0..4; j=0 makes T' a zero-sum in S, and j>0 makes T' * g^(5-j) a zero-sum in S since m(g)=4 >= 5-j; both contradict zero-sum-freeness
P2_inductive_reduction.spot_check: 300 random such classes, 0 failures, quotients hitting all 18 rank-2 classes
P2_inductive_reduction.statement: if g in supp(S) has multiplicity 4 then S = g^4 * T, and the image of T in G/<g> = C_5^2 is a MAXIMAL zero-sum-free sequence of length 8, hence of shape A or B by the rank-2 theorem

cross_classification_identity.statement: every minimal zero-sum U of length 13 equals S*(-sigma(S)) for exactly the |supp(U)| choices S = U minus one element, so #(zero-sum-free length 12) = sum over U of |supp(U)|

T1_projective_squarefreeness.OPEN_CONJECTURE: is every maximal zero-sum-free sequence over C_p^3 projectively squarefree? This is the one regularity found here that looks like a theorem waiting for a proof.
T1_projective_squarefreeness.not_locally_forced: u^2 (2u)^1 is itself zero-sum-free, and the only local constraint is m(u)<=2, m(2u)<=1, yet it never occurs
T1_projective_squarefreeness.scope: two independent complete censuses, about 41 billion sequences, no exception
T1_projective_squarefreeness.statement: supp(S) injects into PG(2,5): no two support elements are scalar multiples

verified_by_exhaustion_census_not_proof.T3: the projective support never contains a full line of PG(2,5)
